rule.rule:
Short Vowel Sounds include:

the A in Dad

the O in Lock

the I in Dip

the E in Bed

and the Y in Gym

You hear the 
short A 
in words like 
Ran
Bat
and Back.

You hear the 
short O 
in words like 
Pop
Got
and Rock

You hear the 
short I 
in words like 
Pin
Bit
and Rick

You hear the 
short U 
in words like 
Run
But
and Buck

You hear the 
short E 
in words like 
Red
Bet
and Peck

Consonant Blends

When two or three consonants sounds are spoken together their sounds overlap and partly blend together. 

Examples: 

S-p in Spit . S-p-l in Split

Short Vowel in Closed Syllable

A single written vowel 
has a short sound
in a closed syllable. 

A syllable is closed
when it ends with
a closing consonant 
or consonant team.

Examples: 
at cat 
etch fetch
in pin
on Don
up pup

A Closed Syllable with the Short /a/ Sound.

A closed syllable is a syllable that ends with a closing consonant or consonant team.

In a closed syllable the letter A has the short /a/ sound. 

Examples: Ran . Had . Hat

The Ending /k/ Sound

The ending /k/ sound is written with the letters C-K after a single short vowel in one syllable words. 

Examples: 

Back . Pick  

Use the letter K after other vowel sounds in one syllable words.

Examples: 

Bake . Beak . Book . Bark

A Closed Syllable with the Short /o/ Sound.

A closed syllable is a syllable that ends with a closing consonant or consonant team.

In a closed syllable the letter O has the short /o/ sound. 

Examples: pop . cot . lock

A Closed Syllable with the Short /u/ Sound.

A closed syllable has a single vowel followed by a closing consonant. In a closed syllable the letter U has the short /u/ sound. 

Examples: run . cut . luck

A Closed Syllable with the Short /i/ Sound.

A closed syllable is a syllable that ends with a closing consonant or consonant team.

In a closed syllable the letter I has the short /i/ sound.

Examples: pin . bit . pick

A Closed Syllable with the Short /e/ Sound.

A closed syllable is a syllable that ends with a closing consonant or consonant team. 

In a closed syllable the letter E has the short /e/ sound. 

Examples: 

Pet . Met . Desk
A closed syllable has a single vowel followed by a closing consonant. Words with two closed syllables act the same. \n\nExamples: Rabbit, Atom, Inlet

rule.rule_title: Three sounds of ED past tense ending.
rule.rule:
ED Past Tense Suffix
The suffix E-D, which makes a verb past tense, has three ways to say it: 
1. /d/ when after a voiced sound. Example: Played
2. /t/ when after a unvoiced sound. Example: Walked
3. /ed/ after a T or D. 
Example: Wanted

rule.rule_title: Double Final Single Consonant when adding Vowel Suffix
rule.rule: -V Suffix = Double C  - Double the last consonant when adding a vowel suffix to multi-syllable  words ending in one vowel followed by one consonant when the syllable before the suffix is accented

Suffix S, ES and 3rd Person  - To make a verb third person (he, she, it) add the ending S unless the word ends with an /s/, /z/, /ch/ or /s/ sound,  or if it changes the meaning of the word; then add E-S. Examples : Runs, Passes, Patches, Wishes, Does.

Suffix S, -ES as Plural To make a word plural add the ending S, unless the word end with the S, Z, CH or SH sound, or if it changes the meaning of the word; then add E-S. Examples: Hits, Boxes, Wishes.

S-H . T-H . W-H

S-H, T-H & W-H are not blends. They each represent one sound. 

Examples: 
SH in Shot and Dish,
TH in Thing and With,
WH in What and Why.
SH at the beginning of any syllable after the first one, except for the ending -ship.

/ch/ Sound Endings

An ending /ch/ sound, after a single short vowel, is written with the letters T-C-H. 
Examples: Catch . Pitch

But after a long vowel sound, or a consonant, it is written with the letters C-H only. 

Examples: Peach . Torch

DGE & GE as /j/ Sound Endings

English words do not end with the letter J.
 
Instead, use D-G-E after a short vowel. The letter D is used as a second consonant, along with the letter G, so that the word's short vowel will remain short. 
Fudge (not \fuge").

The Letter X One Man Team

At the end of a base word the letter X becomes one letter with two sounds.

The /k/ Sound quickly followed by the /s/ Sound.

Examples: Fox, Box

Q-U as /kw/ Sounds

In English words, the letter Q always has the letter U after it. 

Together they make the /k/ and /w/ consonant sounds. 

Words in English that start with a /kw/ blend sound are always spelled with the letters Q-U. 

Examples: Quit, Queen.

U & O-O Short /oo/ Sound Teams

The long /u/ sound can be written with the letter U, the letters E-W and the letters O-O. 


The sound of U in \Put"can be written with the letter U and and with the letters O-O.

The /ng/ Sound

The /ng/ sound is one sound, and written with the letters N & G, at the ends of words.

Examples: Sing, Bang, Running

However, when the /ng/ sound is followed by the /k/ sound it is written with the letter N only.

Examples: Sink, Bank

FF . LL . SS . ZZ

The letters F, L, S and Z are doubled after a single short vowel in a closed syllable. 
They are doubled but each pair have only one sound each. 
Sometimes other letters are doubled as well. 

Examples: Stuff . Mill . Boss . Buzz

rule.rule_title: The All Saw Pa\'s Paunch Pattern
rule.rule:
The /ah/ Sound

The /ah/ sound is usually written with the letters A-W at the end of a base word and with the letters A-U in the middle or the beginning of the word. 

Examples: Paw . Sauce

At the end of a one syllable word the /ah/ sound can sometimes be written with the letter A only.

Examples: Ma . Pa

The letter A before LL, or after W, will have the /ah/ sound.

Examples: Ball . Want . Water
The /oy/ sound is usually written with the letters O-Y at the end of a word and with the letters O-I in the middle or beginning of a word. \n\nExamples: Toy . Toil . Boy . Boil

The /ow/ sound is usually written with the letters O-W at the end of a base word. 

Examples: Now . How

It is usually written with the letters O-U in the middle, or beginning, of a word. 

Examples: Noun . Hound
The letter R, after a short vowel, blends with the vowel to make a new \\R-Controlled\"sound. E-R\
The letter R, after a short vowel, blends with the vowel to make a new \\R-Controlled\"sound.

The letter W before A, A-R & O-R changes the vowel sound. 

The short A sound changes to the AH sound. 

The AR sound changes to an OR sound. 

The OR sound changes to an ER sound. 

Examples: 

Want .  Warm .  Word

rule.rule_title: Long I & O Before Consonant Blends
rule.rule:
Long /i/ & Long /o/ before N-D, L-D, S-T & L-T Blends.

The letters I and O, before the consonant blends N-D, L-D, S-T & L-T, often have the long /i/ and long /o/ sounds. 

Examples: Mild . Cold . Mind . Bolt
The letter C before E, I, or Y makes the /s/ sound. \n\nExamples: Cent, City, Cyber.
The letter G before E, I, or Y usually makes the J sound. \n\nExamples: Gem, Gin, Gym

E Makes Short Vowel Long 
(The First Power of Silent E.) 

Silent E, after a closed syllable, changes a short vowel into a long vowel. The letter E is like a \key"that can \""open\"" a  closed syllable.

E Makes G Soft
(The Second Power of Silent E.)

Silent E can change the Hard G /g/ sound to the soft G /j/ sound.

Examples: Gem . Gym . Range . Large
E Makes Ending Consonant-L Blend \\Legal\
E Makes Ending V \\Legal\"- The Fifth Power of Silent E.
Ending E can be used after an S to make the word not look like a plural word. Examples: Tense, Tease.
o + w, th, m, n, v = Schwa - o can = Schwa in a stressed syllable next to w, th, m, n, v.

rule.rule_title: A Single Long Vowel in an Open Syllable
rule.rule:
A single vowel, in an open syllable, usually has the long sound. 
Except one-syllable words ending in A, and sometimes O. 

Examples: 

Long I in I and By. 
Long O in No. 
Long A in Able. 
Long O in Open 
and long U in Unit.

rule.rule_title: Ending Y with Long E Sound
rule.rule: -y as Long I in one (open)-syllable word ending with y = Long I\n\n-y as long E sound. y = Long E at end of a multi-syllable base word.

rule.rule_title: Y changes to I before Vowel Suffix
rule.rule: Suffix after Y - Change Y to I. Single vowel Y changes to Y when adding any ending, unless the ending begins with I.

The A-Y & A-I Long /a/ Sound Teams

The long /a/ sound is usually written as A-Y at the end of a base word 
and as A-I in the middle or the beginning. 

Examples: 

Pay . Pain . May . Main . Delay

EE & EA Long /e/ Sound Teams

The letter E before the letter E
or the letter E before the letter I both make the Long /e/ sound.

Examples: Eel . Eat

I-E & I-G-H Long /i/ Sound Teams

The letter I before the letter E 
or the letter I before the letters G-H have the Long /i/ sound. 

Examples: Pie . High

O before A, O before W and O before E can make the Long /O/ sound. 

Examples: Toad, Grow, Toe

Long U and E-W & O-O Long /u/ Sound Teams

The long /u/ sound can be written with the letter U, the letters E-W and the letters O-O. 

Examples: 

Rule . New . Boot

U-E & E-W /ew/ Sound Teams

The /ew/ sound can be written with the letters E-U and the letters E-W. 

Examples: Due . Few

rule.rule_title: U before E or E before W
rule.rule: U before E or E before W makes the Long /U/ sound. \n\nExamples: Few, Due.

rule.rule_title: I with Long E Sound in Open Syllable
rule.rule: I with Long E Sound in Open Syllable

Open Syllable Long /i/ Sound

In multi-syllable (multisyllabic) words the long /i/ sound is most often written with the letter I in an open syllable.

Examples: item . idea . multisyllabic
INE with Short I Sound
AIN with Short I Sound

rule.rule_title: T.I as SH Sound before O.N.
rule.rule:
T-I in T-I-O-N with the /sh/ Sound Team

The letters T-I often have the /sh/ sound in T-I-O-N in multisyllabic words.

Examples: Action . Nation . Administration

rule.rule_title: SI as SH Sound before O.N.
rule.rule:
S-I in S-I-O-N with the /sh/ Sound Team

The letters S-I often have the /sh/ sound in S-I-O-N in multisyllabic words.

Examples: Passion . Mission . Recession
When T is followed by UR in the middle of a word  the R sound changes the T to a CH as the tongue is pulled back in the mouth. Examples: nature . mutual . Legislature . \

PH as F Sound

PH with an F sound coms to English from Greek. In ancient times it had a P sound but changed over time.

Examples: phone . alphabet . triumph

CH as SH Sound

CH with an SH sound comes to English from French. French does not have the CH sound. It uses CH for the SH sound.

Examples: chef . machine . brochure

CH as K Sound

CH with an K sound comes to English from Greek. Greek does not have the CH sound nor the SH sound. But it does have the K sound.

Examples: chaos . archive . stomach

rule.rule_title: C.I, T.I as SH Sound before O.U.S.
rule.rule:
CI (CIOUS), TI (TIOUS) as SH Sound

C-I  in C-I-O-U-S and T-I in T-I-O-U-S with the /sh/ Sound

The letters C-I and the letters T-I can have the /sh/ sound  in multisyllabic words that end with I-O-U-S.

Examples: vicious . delicious . fictitious . nutritious

rule.rule_title: CI, TI as SH Sound before A.N.
rule.rule:
CI & TI as SH Sound before AN

C-I & in C-I-A-N and T-I in T-I-A-N with the /sh/ Sound

The letters C-I and the letters T-I can have the /sh/ sound in C-I-A-N and in T-I-A-L multisyllabic words.

Examples: Electrician . Magician . Martian

rule.rule_title: CI, TI as SH Sound before A.L.
rule.rule:
CI (CIAL) & TI (TIAL) as SH Sound

C-I & in C-I-A-L and T-I in T-I-A-L with the /sh/ Sound

The letters C-I and the letters T-I can have the /sh/ sound in C-I-A-L and in C-I-A-L multisyllabic words.

Examples: official . crucial . initial . partial

rule.rule_title: TI as SH or CH Sound after N, before A.L.
rule.rule:
T-I in N-T-I-A-L with the /sh/ Sound

The letters T-I can have the /ch/ sound in N-T-I-A-L in multisyllabic words.

Examples: 

Potential . Preferential

rule.rule_title: G.E, S.I, S.U. as Voiced ZH Sound
rule.rule:
G-E, S-I, S-U as Voiced /sh/ Sound.

G-E, S-I and S-U can make the Voiced SH Sound as in beige, vision and treasure.

Examples: rouge . Asia . closure

rule.rule_title: Silent Letters. g.N, G.h, G.u, h.O, k.N, p.S.
rule.rule:
Silent Letters in gN, Gh, Gu, hO, kN, pS Teams

G is silent when followed by N in the beginning of a word.
Example: gnarl.
H is silent when it comes after the letter G in the beginning of a word.
Example: ghost.
U is silent when it comes after the letter G in the beginning of a word. The silent U makes the letter G have the hard /g/ sound.
Example: guest.
H is silent when followed by O in the beginning of a word.
Example: honest.
K is silent when followed by N in the beginning of a word.
Example: knee.
P is silent when followed by S in the beginning of a word.
Example: psychology.

rule.rule_title: Silent Letters. S.c, S.w, w.H, w.R.
rule.rule:
Silent Letters in Sc, Sw, wH & wR Teams

C is silent when it comes after the letter S in the beginning of many words, or syllables, that come to English from Latin.
Examples: science . obscene.
W is occasionally silent when it comes after the letter S in the beginning of some words or syllables.
Examples: sword . answer.
W is silent when followed by H in the beginning of a word.
Examples: whose . whole.
W is silent when followed by R in the beginning of a word.
Examples: write . wrist.

rule.rule_title: Silent Letters. M.b, b.T, M.n, g.N.
rule.rule:
Silent Letters in Mb, bT, Mn, gN Teams

B is silent when it comes after the letter M at the end of words.
Examples: climb . thumb.
B is also silent when it comes before the letter T at the end of words.
Examples: debt . doubt.
G is silent when it comes before the letter N at the end of words.
Examples: column . hymn.
M is silent when it comes before the letter N at the end of words.
Examples: sign . campaign.

rule.rule_title: Silent Letters. F.t, S.t, t.L.e, Q.u.e.
rule.rule:
Silent Letters in Ft, St, tLe, Que Teams

T is silent when it comes after the letter F in the middle of words.
Examples: listen . often.
T is also silent when it comes after the letter S in the middle of words.
Examples: fasten . moisten.
T is silent when it comes before the letters L and E at the end of words.
Examples: castle . wrestle.
U and E are often silent when they come after the letter Q at the end of words; words that typically come to English from French.
Examples: antique . grotesque.
O.U.G.H (F)\n\nIn Old English the letters GH were written for the sound \\KH\"which sounds like a K followed by an H made at the back of the mouth.
th -e = voiced - e after th = voiced TH

sec.sec_desc: Keys is a systematic introduction to the keyboard, starting with the Home Row, and including all letter keys. In this section, the keys are matched individually with their most common sounds. The vowels are short. The C Key makes the ?k? sound, etc.
Short introduces the same sounds within real words; phoneme by phoneme. The first digraph (ck) is introduced, as well as, two syllable words with the suffixes s, es, ed, en and ic.
Blends introduces words with consonant blends such as st-, tr-, sm-, dr-, -nd, etc.

Consonant Teams introduces consonant teams such as sh, th. wh, ch, tch, dge, qu, x ng, as well as introducing the prefix mis-, in-, un- and Double Consonants before suffixes -ed and -ing (top /topped / topping).

Vowel Teams introduces short vowel teams such as au, aw. oi, oy, ou, ow, oo, as well as introducing the prefixes: con-, dis-, ex-, ad-, an-, en-, em-, and the suffixes: -ful, -less, -ness, -ess, -let, -ive.

Mixed Teams introduces vowel/consonant teams such as R-Controlled vowels (er, ir, ur, ar, or), W-Controlled (wa-, wor- war-), and Sort C and G, as well as introducing the prefixes: non-  and the suffixes: -er, -est, -ine.

E Power introduces the powers of the letter E to influence the sounds of other letters. Silent E to make a short vowel long (mat -mate), make Cand G soft (dance, change), make L and V ?legal? (able and love).
Long Vowels focuses on long vowel sounds mostly in multisyllabic words and including long a,e,i,o,u and y (with long i or e sounds).\n
Long Vowel Teams introduces on long vowel teams such as ai, ay, ee, ea, igh, ie, oe, ow, oa, ew, ue.)
Vowels focuses on the less common vowel sound graphemes such as -a in Mama, -i- in radio, and -y in happy, -i-ne in examine and ?ai-n in certain.
Expert Teams 1 focusing on both consonant and consonant-vowel teams found mostly in multisyllabic words such as -ti-, -si-,ci with the sh sound.

Expert Teams 2 focusing on both consonant and consonant-vowel teams found mostly in multisyllabic words such as -ti-, -si-,ci with the sh sound, tu- and -ti- with the ch sound, ph with the f sound and ch with the sh and k sounds.
Silent Letter Teams focuses silent letter teams such as gh in ghost, gu in guard, bt in debt, and ps in psychology.
